messages.lore.book_bed_ledger.author: an unnamed attendant before the Dawn
messages.lore.book_bed_ledger.text:
Twelve beds. Twelve clean blankets. Eleven cups.

Apprentice took a cup downstairs. Remind him tomorrow.

Twelve beds. Thirteen blankets. Someone expects company.

Instructions arrived from the Office. We are to keep everyone in their assigned places until the ceremony ends.

Twelve beds. Twelve blankets. No one sleeping.

Count again in the morning.
messages.lore.book_bed_ledger.title: The Bed Counter's Ledger
messages.lore.book_final_atlas.author: the Unclosed Office, unsigned circular
messages.lore.book_final_atlas.text:
Each road shall receive a destination. Each settlement shall receive a place. Each border shall receive an owner.

Unregistered valleys must be reported before dawn. Reports received after dawn will be considered impossible and returned to their sender.

Please refrain from moving during the completion ceremony. The Office cannot accept responsibility for persons entered under the wrong country.

Tomorrow, the map will be finished.
messages.lore.book_final_atlas.title: Instructions for the Final Atlas
messages.lore.book_handles.author: Pella of the Blue Handle
messages.lore.book_handles.text:
My first handle was chosen by the woman who made me. It was a good handle. I used it for thirty years.

When it broke, the mender asked what kind I wanted. Nobody had asked before.

I chose blue. My maker would have preferred green. I think we could have discussed it over tea.

I would have poured.
messages.lore.book_handles.title: On the Ownership of Handles
messages.lore.book_waiting_cup.author: a Hearthkeeper's household, copied anonymously
messages.lore.book_waiting_cup.text:
We used to set an extra place at supper for travelers. Then we had three travelers and only one spare plate. Grandmother said the custom needed improvement.

Now we keep a clean cup beside the door. Whoever comes next may use it. Whoever comes after that may wash it.

Grandmother called this hospitality. Grandfather called it a successful division of labor. They agreed for nearly sixty years.
messages.lore.book_waiting_cup.title: A Cup for Whoever Comes Next
messages.lore.book_warm_letter.author: Iven, recipient unnamed
messages.lore.book_warm_letter.text:
I charged the scarf at the inn. It will keep its warmth until morning. There is a loose thread beside the clasp, so pull gently.

You said I never remember practical things. I remembered the scarf, the bread, and your terrible little spoon.

I meant to remember a better goodbye. You will have to accept this one until I return.
messages.lore.book_warm_letter.title: A Letter Kept Warm
messages.lore.book_water_notes.author: caravan mender Sef Dapple
messages.lore.book_water_notes.text:
Shade the jar before you shade your boots. Boots complain less expensively.

Repair a crack before the journey. A cup repaired halfway across the wastes becomes a meeting of everybody's opinions.

I have seen a rain jar emptied by a careless child and by a very careful adult. The child admitted it sooner.
messages.lore.book_water_notes.title: Notes on Keeping Water
messages.lore.citizen_fallback_bye_01_v05.text: May you find a way home.
messages.lore.citizen_fallback_hello_01_v04.text: Hello there. Safe road so far?
messages.lore.citizen_fallback_hello_01_v06.text: Come in from the road for a moment.
messages.lore.citizen_fallback_topic_01.text: I don't know enough to tell you.
messages.lore.citizen_fallback_topic_01_v02.text: I've only heard pieces of that story.
messages.lore.citizen_fallback_topic_01_v03.text: You'd need someone who knows more than I do.
messages.lore.citizen_fallback_topic_01_v04.text: I don't have a useful account of that.
messages.lore.citizen_fallback_topic_01_v05.text: I'd rather leave that question to someone who was there.
messages.lore.citizen_fallback_topic_01_v06.text: I couldn't tell you with any certainty.
messages.lore.delver_bye_01_v02.text: Keep the return route clear in your head.
messages.lore.delver_bye_01_v03.text: Come back with enough strength for the last stretch.
messages.lore.delver_bye_01_v04.text: Go carefully, and remember the stairs.
messages.lore.delver_bye_01_v05.text: Leave a little of yourself for the journey home.
messages.lore.delver_bye_01_v06.text: Good travels. You still have to come back from them.
messages.lore.delver_delivery_active.text: A delivery to sort. Lift with both hands. Looking brave is no help to a dropped crate.
messages.lore.delver_delivery_active_v02.text: They're sorting a delivery. Two hands to a crate, please.
messages.lore.delver_delivery_active_v03.text: A delivery to sort. Keep a good hold before trying to look impressive.
messages.lore.delver_delivery_active_v04.text: Those crates need carrying. Bravery isn't a substitute for both hands.
messages.lore.delver_delivery_active_v05.text: We're sorting the delivery. A dropped crate doesn't care what you meant to prove.
messages.lore.delver_delivery_active_v06.text: The square has a delivery to sort. Hold the weight properly before taking a step.
messages.lore.delver_delivery_finished.text: The delivery has been received. A stack of crates that stays where you put it is a pleasant surprise.
messages.lore.delver_delivery_finished_v02.text: The crates have arrived. I appreciate supplies that stay where they're set down.
messages.lore.delver_delivery_finished_v03.text: Delivery received. None of those crates has tried to follow me. I like that.
messages.lore.delver_delivery_finished_v04.text: The delivery is in. A quiet stack is an agreeable neighbor.
messages.lore.delver_delivery_finished_v05.text: The crates are staying in the square for now. Predictable cargo makes a pleasant change.
messages.lore.delver_delivery_finished_v06.text: Everything's arrived. Those stacks are behaving better than some things I've met underground.
messages.lore.delver_guild_01.text: Your journal needs a way back as much as it needs a new discovery. Mark the stairs before you admire the ceiling.
messages.lore.delver_guild_01_v02.text: Give the return route as much ink as the new discovery.
messages.lore.delver_guild_01_v03.text: Mark the stairs for your guildmates before you write about the fine ceiling.
messages.lore.delver_guild_01_v04.text: Your journal should help someone get home from the place you're describing.
messages.lore.delver_guild_01_v05.text: A page about a mystery is useful. So is the page that tells you how to leave.
messages.lore.delver_guild_01_v06.text: Leave the next Milewarden a way back. The marvel can have its own paragraph afterward.
messages.lore.delver_hello_01.text: Sit if you're staying. My neck has retired, too.
messages.lore.delver_hello_01_v02.text: Sit down. My neck gets tired before the conversation does.
messages.lore.delver_hello_01_v03.text: If you've got a story, bring it down to sitting height.
messages.lore.delver_hello_01_v04.text: I've retired from craning my neck. Take a seat.
messages.lore.delver_hello_01_v05.text: You can stand if you like. I'll be listening from here.
messages.lore.delver_hello_01_v06.text: Staying a while? Sit. The road won't object.
messages.lore.delver_mage_01.text: Blink still needs somewhere clear to put you. Remember that when you're frightened.
messages.lore.delver_mage_01_v02.text: Blink needs a clear place to arrive. Fear doesn't make more room.
messages.lore.delver_mage_01_v03.text: Before you Blink, look where you'll stand afterward.
messages.lore.delver_mage_01_v04.text: A wall stays solid when you're frightened. Blink toward clear ground.
messages.lore.delver_mage_01_v05.text: Find your landing place before you cast Blink.
messages.lore.delver_mage_01_v06.text: Blink can get you out of trouble if you leave it somewhere clear to put you.
messages.lore.delver_memory_01.text: My old crew argued over every meal. I miss the noise.
messages.lore.delver_memory_01_v02.text: My crew could turn supper into an argument. I still miss hearing them.
messages.lore.delver_memory_01_v03.text: I miss my old crew most at mealtimes. Nobody here argues quite the same way.
messages.lore.delver_memory_01_v04.text: We argued over every meal on the road. I'd gladly hear it again.
messages.lore.delver_memory_01_v05.text: A quiet supper makes me remember my crew. We were never quiet over food.
messages.lore.delver_memory_01_v06.text: My companions found something to disagree about at every meal. I miss those voices.
messages.lore.delver_neighbors_01.text: My old crew brought five flags and one cooking pot. We learned which one mattered when it rained.
messages.lore.delver_neighbors_01_v02.text: My crew carried five flags and a single cooking pot. Rain taught us which to worry about.
messages.lore.delver_neighbors_01_v03.text: Five flags in our packs. One cooking pot. We kept the pot dry first.
messages.lore.delver_neighbors_01_v04.text: We brought five flags on the road and cooked in one pot. Bad weather made us practical.
messages.lore.delver_neighbors_01_v05.text: Rain didn't care about our five flags. Supper depended on the one pot.
messages.lore.delver_neighbors_01_v06.text: Our crew had five flags between us and one cooking pot. We all agreed about the pot when the rain came.
messages.lore.delver_ruin_01.text: A gate opening is a chance to leave as well as a chance to go deeper.
messages.lore.delver_ruin_01_v02.text: When a gate opens, remember the way out.
messages.lore.delver_ruin_01_v03.text: An open gate gives you a choice. Leaving is one of them.
messages.lore.delver_ruin_01_v04.text: You needn't go deeper every time you can.
messages.lore.delver_ruin_01_v05.text: A gate that lets you onward also gives you a moment to decide.
messages.lore.delver_ruin_01_v06.text: Take a breath at an open gate. Going home is still a journey.
messages.lore.delver_supper_active.text: Supper is being set out. No helmets at the table. That rule took my old crew years to learn.
messages.lore.delver_supper_active_v02.text: Supper's being laid out. Helmets can sit somewhere else.
messages.lore.delver_supper_active_v03.text: There's a meal going out. Take the helmet off before you lean over a bowl.
messages.lore.delver_supper_active_v04.text: They're setting supper. My crew needed years to learn that helmets weren't tableware.
messages.lore.delver_supper_active_v05.text: Supper beside the fountain. I hope nobody brings a helmet to the table.
messages.lore.delver_supper_active_v06.text: The table is being laid. We can eat without armor getting a place of its own.
messages.lore.delver_supper_finished.text: Supper is over. The cups are drying. Nobody argued about watch duty. I could get used to that.
messages.lore.delver_supper_finished_v02.text: Supper's over. A quiet meal with no watch-duty argument still surprises me.
messages.lore.delver_supper_finished_v03.text: The cups are drying, and nobody has assigned me the late watch. Good evening.
messages.lore.delver_supper_finished_v04.text: We've finished eating. I enjoyed hearing no quarrel about who stayed awake afterward.
messages.lore.delver_supper_finished_v05.text: The meal ended pleasantly. Nobody tried to trade watch duty for the last serving.
messages.lore.delver_supper_finished_v06.text: Supper's finished. A clean cup and no watch roster make a fine end to it.
messages.lore.delver_sword_01.text: A sword arm needs rest. Pride can wait beside it.
messages.lore.delver_sword_01_v02.text: Rest the arm that holds the sword. You'll need it again.
messages.lore.delver_sword_01_v03.text: A tired sword arm deserves a pause.
messages.lore.delver_sword_01_v04.text: Your pride can keep watch while your sword arm rests.
messages.lore.delver_sword_01_v05.text: Give that arm time before the next fight.
messages.lore.delver_sword_01_v06.text: There's no shame in resting the hand you rely on.
messages.lore.delver_world_01.text: I once slept below a tower built for a sky with two moons. Its roof kept our rain out well enough.
messages.lore.delver_world_01_v02.text: I slept beneath a tower made for two moons once. Its roof was quite good at keeping out our rain.
messages.lore.delver_world_01_v03.text: That old tower had two moons in its carvings. I slept there dry enough beneath our sky.
messages.lore.delver_world_01_v04.text: A tower from a two-moon world gave me shelter once. The roof didn't mind the difference.
messages.lore.delver_world_01_v05.text: I once found a dry place under a tower whose builders knew two moons. A good roof travels well between worlds.
messages.lore.delver_world_01_v06.text: The tower I slept under was built beneath a sky with two moons. Our rain still stayed outside.
messages.lore.discovery_borrowed_refuge.author: A traveler from {city_name}
messages.lore.discovery_borrowed_refuge.text:
We borrowed this cart for the road from {city_name}. When its wheel broke, we made a shelter of it. When the rain ended, we left the shelter for the next person.

The keeper called that a poor way to return a cart. The mender called it a useful second career.

Our last destination was {dungeon_name}. We left the name here so nobody would have to guess which ruin we meant.
messages.lore.discovery_borrowed_refuge.title: A Place Left for Someone
messages.lore.discovery_root_register.author: An unsigned woodland register
messages.lore.discovery_root_register.text:
The roots took the lower shelves first. We moved the books upstairs. The branches took the upper shelves next. We stopped calling it damage.

{city_name} keeps the living names. This register keeps a few older ones. Both lists have room for another entry.

Under {dungeon_name}, someone wrote that the trees remember every visitor. Someone else crossed it out. The ink has faded; the crossing-out has not.
messages.lore.discovery_root_register.title: The Root Register
messages.lore.discovery_survey_marker.author: A Milewarden's field note
messages.lore.discovery_survey_marker.text:
This stone was measured twice. The first surveyor counted the road from {city_name}. The second counted the footsteps of everyone who had walked it.

Their figures disagreed. Their stone did not move.

The margin names {dungeon_name}. A Milewarden has added: I am taking a fresh sheet. If the old surveyors kept a third account there, I mean to bring a copy home.
messages.lore.discovery_survey_marker.title: The Second Measure
messages.lore.discovery_watchpost_notice.author: An old survey office
messages.lore.discovery_watchpost_notice.text:
All journeys beginning at {city_name} must name their destination. Any traveler bound for {dungeon_name} must also name the destination after that.

Blank lines are provided below.

A later hand has written: leave one blank. It gives the road somewhere to go.
messages.lore.discovery_watchpost_notice.title: Notice for an Unfinished Journey
messages.lore.history_borrowed_light.author: The local archive of {city_name}
messages.lore.history_borrowed_light.book_text: Beside the lamp entries, a later hand wrote: clean the glass before you pass it on. Underneath, in smaller letters: yes, you too.
The crates arrived. A neighbor wiped down the borrowed tools before passing them to the next pair of hands.
After supper, someone washed the cups while another dried them. The keeper put a clean lamp beside the next stack.
messages.lore.history_borrowed_light.landmark_tex: The road marker carries a lamp-shaped scratch. The ledger says a light can belong to a route, even while one person holds it.
messages.lore.history_borrowed_light.text: In {city_name}, a winter ledger follows a lamp from house to house. Each keeper wrote who would need it next. The last old entry names {dungeon_name}; below it, someone has drawn an empty hook.
messages.lore.history_borrowed_light.title: The Borrowed Light
messages.lore.history_borrowed_light.witness_text: We say the light is borrowed, even when we made the lamp ourselves. Someone will need it after us. My grandmother showed me the entry for {dungeon_name}. She made me clean the glass too.
messages.lore.history_returned_names.author: The local archive of {city_name}
messages.lore.history_returned_names.book_text: The town copy records a keeper refusing to close the register. A name could be corrected by its owner. Nobody else was allowed to decide that a journey was finished.
The delivery arrived. The receiver signed the ledger, then asked the carter whether anyone was waiting for them at home.
At supper, the keeper learned a traveler's name. By the time the cups were gathered, half the table was using it.
messages.lore.history_returned_names.landmark_tex: Names cut beside the road have a second, smaller line underneath. Most are empty. Beside one, someone carved: I came back. I still like my name.
messages.lore.history_returned_names.text: The oldest register in {city_name} leaves space after every name. It began with travelers going to {dungeon_name}; the empty space was meant for whatever they would call themselves on return. The town kept the custom when the ink faded.
messages.lore.history_returned_names.title: Names Kept for Returning
messages.lore.history_returned_names.witness_text: We keep a space for the returning name. If you visit {dungeon_name}, come back and tell us what you'd put there. Leave it empty if you like. I'll be glad to see you either way.
messages.lore.history_shared_measure.author: The local archive of {city_name}
messages.lore.history_shared_measure.book_text: A local margin explains the same measure. A filled water jar counts as one interval; a closed door counts as none. The keeper still asks households to leave room for a traveler.
The carter delivered the supplies. Before counting the crates, a neighbor brought them water and a stool.
The supper table is clear again. One stool stayed empty until a late traveler arrived. Nobody had to ask for it.
messages.lore.history_shared_measure.landmark_tex: The roadside marks belong to that survey. Their spacing measures the help a traveler could expect, rather than the length of a stride.
messages.lore.history_shared_measure.text: The old survey at {city_name} counted water jars and places to rest along the road. Its last entry names {dungeon_name}. A later warden added a question beside it: who will open the door?
messages.lore.history_shared_measure.title: The Shared Measure
messages.lore.history_shared_measure.witness_text: My grandparents argued over the numbers, but both left water by the door. The register ends at {dungeon_name}. I wonder who was there to meet the last surveyor.
messages.lore.keeper_bye_01.text: Come back when you need somewhere to sit.
messages.lore.keeper_bye_01_v02.text: There's a place to rest when you come back.
messages.lore.keeper_bye_01_v03.text: Go well. I'll be here when the road tires you out.
messages.lore.keeper_bye_01_v04.text: Come back with whatever story you can carry.
messages.lore.keeper_bye_01_v05.text: Rest here again when you need it.
messages.lore.keeper_bye_01_v06.text: Safe travels. We'll make room for you on your return.
messages.lore.keeper_dawn_01.text: My grandmother said the Dawn lasted three days. Her sister said four. They argued until sunset.
messages.lore.keeper_dawn_01_v02.text: Grandmother counted three days of Dawn. Her sister counted four. Neither would let the other have the last word.
messages.lore.keeper_dawn_01_v03.text: Our family has two accounts of the Dawn: three days and four. Both are in the same book.
messages.lore.keeper_dawn_01_v04.text: Grandmother insisted the Dawn lasted three days. Her sister added a fourth every time she told it.
messages.lore.keeper_dawn_01_v05.text: Three days, Grandmother said. Four, said her sister. Their argument lasted longer than either account.
messages.lore.keeper_dawn_01_v06.text: I've copied both family accounts of the Dawn. If I choose three days or four, somebody's ghost will complain.
messages.lore.keeper_delivery_active.text: A delivery is being sorted in the square. I offered to count the crates. They said I should count cups instead.
messages.lore.keeper_delivery_active_v02.text: We're sorting a delivery in the square. Apparently my cup-counting doesn't qualify me to count crates.
messages.lore.keeper_delivery_active_v03.text: The crates are being sorted. I offered to help and was sent back to the cups.
messages.lore.keeper_delivery_active_v04.text: A delivery's in the square. They know what belongs where better than I do.
messages.lore.keeper_delivery_active_v05.text: They're sorting the delivery. I shall stick to vessels I can carry in one hand.
messages.lore.keeper_delivery_active_v06.text: The square is busy with crates. I offered to count them. My reputation for cups arrived before I did.
messages.lore.keeper_delivery_finished.text: The delivery has been received. Those crates can wait a little while. Tired hands make poor knots.
messages.lore.keeper_delivery_finished_v02.text: The delivery's here. Let tired hands rest before tying another knot.
messages.lore.keeper_delivery_finished_v03.text: Those crates have arrived safely. They can wait while the people who carried them sit down.
messages.lore.keeper_delivery_finished_v04.text: The sorting is done for now. A crate has more patience than a tired back.
messages.lore.keeper_delivery_finished_v05.text: We've received the delivery. I hope its carriers find a seat before finding another job.
messages.lore.keeper_delivery_finished_v06.text: The crates are in. There's time to rest before deciding which one to lift next.
messages.lore.keeper_fountain_01.text: The fountain offers rest. Keeping the steps clean is my contribution.
messages.lore.keeper_fountain_01_v02.text: People come here worn out. I keep the steps clear so they can sit.
messages.lore.keeper_fountain_01_v03.text: The water does its work. I do the sweeping.
messages.lore.keeper_fountain_01_v04.text: Rest by the fountain. You needn't earn a place beside it.
messages.lore.keeper_fountain_01_v05.text: I tend the fountain and make sure there's room around it. Some days that means moving a very stubborn crate.
messages.lore.keeper_fountain_01_v06.text: The fountain has heard more road stories than I have. I still like listening.
messages.lore.keeper_frost_01.text: Some bells are waiting for people, too.
messages.lore.keeper_frost_01_v02.text: A wrapped bell can wait a long time.
messages.lore.keeper_frost_01_v03.text: Some bells stay quiet until their traveler comes home.
messages.lore.keeper_frost_01_v04.text: We keep a bell for people we hope to see again.
messages.lore.keeper_frost_01_v05.text: There's waiting in a quiet bell.
messages.lore.keeper_frost_01_v06.text: A bell needn't ring to remind us of someone.
messages.lore.keeper_guild_01.text: Your guild keeps asking what's beyond the next hill. I keep a cup here for when you come back to tell me.
messages.lore.keeper_guild_01_v02.text: Milewardens come back with new names for faraway places. I make sure there's a seat when they tell us.
messages.lore.keeper_guild_01_v03.text: Your maps go farther than my errands. Bring me a story when you return.
messages.lore.keeper_guild_01_v04.text: The guild can keep its ink. I'll keep a cup ready for the hand that brings it home.
messages.lore.keeper_guild_01_v05.text: You and your guildmates always want another road. I want to hear how you got back from it.
messages.lore.keeper_guild_01_v06.text: When a Milewarden returns, we hear about country nobody here has seen. I like to be ready for that.
messages.lore.keeper_hello_01.text: Welcome to {city_name}. Take a breath. The road can wait.
messages.lore.keeper_hello_01_v02.text: You've reached {city_name}. Come out of the road and catch your breath.
messages.lore.keeper_hello_01_v03.text: Welcome to {city_name}. There's no need to tell your story standing up.
messages.lore.keeper_hello_01_v04.text: {city_name} has room for another traveler. Start with a little rest.
messages.lore.keeper_hello_01_v05.text: First time in {city_name}? Rest your feet before you decide where to go next.
messages.lore.keeper_hello_01_v06.text: This is {city_name}. You're welcome here. The dust on your boots can wait.
messages.lore.keeper_hello_02.text: Rest first. You can tell me what happened afterward.
messages.lore.keeper_hello_02_v02.text: Sit for a moment. News keeps better than tired legs.
messages.lore.keeper_hello_02_v03.text: You can finish that story after you've rested.
messages.lore.keeper_hello_02_v04.text: Let the road have a minute without you. Take a seat.
messages.lore.keeper_hello_02_v05.text: Rest your hands. Whatever happened, you don't have to tell it all at once.
messages.lore.keeper_hello_02_v06.text: You look as though you've carried the journey far enough for today.
messages.lore.keeper_meadow_01.text: We set a place for whoever the road brings next.
messages.lore.keeper_meadow_01_v02.text: Leave a place open. The road hasn't sent everyone yet.
messages.lore.keeper_meadow_01_v03.text: There's a cup for whoever reaches us next.
messages.lore.keeper_meadow_01_v04.text: Someone we haven't met will need a seat.
messages.lore.keeper_meadow_01_v05.text: We can make room when the next traveler comes.
messages.lore.keeper_meadow_01_v06.text: Keep one place ready for a stranger.
messages.lore.keeper_neighbors_01.text: We argue over who should mend a road. Then someone's child walks it, and suddenly everyone has a shovel.
messages.lore.keeper_neighbors_01_v02.text: Everyone has an opinion about a road until it needs mending. A child walking it usually settles the matter.
messages.lore.keeper_neighbors_01_v03.text: A broken road becomes public business as soon as someone we know has to use it.
messages.lore.keeper_neighbors_01_v04.text: Neighbors can quarrel all morning and share a shovel before supper.
messages.lore.keeper_neighbors_01_v05.text: The loudest argument about a road often comes from two people who will mend it together.
messages.lore.keeper_neighbors_01_v06.text: People disagree about who should do the work. They agree they want their neighbors to get home.
messages.lore.keeper_return_01.text: Back from {dungeon_name}? Sit down before you tell me about it.
messages.lore.keeper_return_01_v02.text: You made it back from {dungeon_name}. Rest first; I can listen afterward.
messages.lore.keeper_return_01_v03.text: Back from {dungeon_name}? I was hoping to hear your steps again.
messages.lore.keeper_return_01_v04.text: Leave {dungeon_name} outside for a moment. You're back among neighbors.
messages.lore.keeper_return_01_v05.text: I've been wondering about your trip to {dungeon_name}. Sit while you tell me.
messages.lore.keeper_return_01_v06.text: So {dungeon_name} let you come home. Take a breath before the account.
messages.lore.keeper_supper_active.text: We are setting out supper by the fountain. There is always room for another cup.
messages.lore.keeper_supper_active_v02.text: We're laying supper out by the fountain. Pull up a place while there's one spare.
messages.lore.keeper_supper_active_v03.text: Come eat with us by the fountain. I can find another cup.
messages.lore.keeper_supper_active_v04.text: There's supper to set out and a traveler to fit in. That sounds right to me.
messages.lore.keeper_supper_active_v05.text: We're making room for supper. Bring yourself; we'll sort out the cups.
messages.lore.keeper_supper_active_v06.text: Supper is going out beside the fountain. A guest is easier to find than an excuse for an empty place.
messages.lore.keeper_supper_finished.text: Supper has finished. We leave the cups out to dry. Someone always remembers one more story while washing up.
messages.lore.keeper_supper_finished_v02.text: The meal is over. The washing-up keeps producing more conversation.
messages.lore.keeper_supper_finished_v03.text: Supper's finished, and the cups are drying. Somebody is still telling the story they started at the table.
messages.lore.keeper_supper_finished_v04.text: We cleared supper away. Nobody seems ready to clear the last story away.
messages.lore.keeper_supper_finished_v05.text: The cups are washed after supper. A few neighbors linger over the drying cloths.
messages.lore.keeper_supper_finished_v06.text: Supper has ended. I leave the cups out while people finish talking.
messages.lore.keeper_world_01.text: When the worlds came together, my family brought a kettle and the name of their village. We've replaced the kettle twice. We still use the name.
messages.lore.keeper_world_01_v02.text: My family's village name survived the collapse. Their kettle lasted less well. We're on the third one now.
messages.lore.keeper_world_01_v03.text: When the worlds joined, my family kept their village's name and brought their kettle. Two kettles later, the name remains.
messages.lore.keeper_world_01_v04.text: The kettle my family carried from their old world is gone. So is its replacement. We still greet people with the old village name.
messages.lore.keeper_world_01_v05.text: My family brought a village name and a kettle into the Endless World. The name has needed fewer repairs.
messages.lore.keeper_world_01_v06.text: We call this place by the village name my family saved at the collapse. The kettle they brought has been replaced twice.
messages.lore.mender_bye_01.text: Mind the corners on your way out.
messages.lore.mender_bye_01_v02.text: Watch the corners. Fresh work deserves a little care.
messages.lore.mender_bye_01_v04.text: Safe travels. Give your seams a look before you leave.
messages.lore.mender_bye_01_v05.text: Mind the edges on the road.
messages.lore.mender_bye_01_v06.text: Take care of the things that carry you.
messages.lore.mender_delivery_active.text: A local delivery to sort. First the bindings, then the contents. A damaged handle tells you where to start.
messages.lore.mender_delivery_active_v02.text: The delivery's being sorted. I look at the bindings before I look inside.
messages.lore.mender_delivery_active_v03.text: They're sorting crates. A worn handle usually tells me where to begin.
messages.lore.mender_delivery_active_v04.text: A delivery in the square. First I check what held it together on the road.
messages.lore.mender_delivery_active_v05.text: The crates are being sorted. Look at their straps before trusting their weight.
messages.lore.mender_delivery_active_v06.text: We're sorting the delivery. Good contents still need sound handles.
messages.lore.mender_delivery_finished.text: The delivery has been received. Those crates will stay here while we decide where everything belongs.
messages.lore.mender_delivery_finished_v02.text: The delivery has arrived. We'll leave the crates here until there's a place for their contents.
messages.lore.mender_delivery_finished_v03.text: Those crates are received. Unpacking can wait until we know where to put things.
messages.lore.mender_delivery_finished_v04.text: The delivery's in. I'd rather plan a shelf than empty a crate onto the ground.
messages.lore.mender_delivery_finished_v05.text: The crates will stand here for now. Deciding where things belong takes longer than opening them.
messages.lore.mender_delivery_finished_v06.text: We've received everything. The square can hold the crates while we sort out their next homes.
messages.lore.mender_guild_01.text: If your guild writes about a strange old tool, draw the handle too. Someone held it. I'd like to know how.
messages.lore.mender_guild_01_v02.text: When you draw an old tool for the guild, show me the worn parts. That's where the hands were.
messages.lore.mender_guild_01_v03.text: Copy the handle as carefully as the mysterious marks. Somebody had to hold the thing.
messages.lore.mender_guild_01_v04.text: Your guild can tell me where a tool was found. I'd also like to know how its owner used it.
messages.lore.mender_guild_01_v05.text: If you bring back a sketch, leave room for the grip and the repairs.
messages.lore.mender_guild_01_v06.text: A strange tool still has weight and edges. Put those in your account; a mender will thank you.
messages.lore.mender_hello_01.text: Let me finish this seam. It has strong opinions.
messages.lore.mender_hello_01_v02.text: One moment. This seam keeps opening where I thought I'd finished.
messages.lore.mender_hello_01_v03.text: Let me tie this off before we talk.
messages.lore.mender_hello_01_v04.text: Hold your story a moment. I'm trying to persuade these edges to meet.
messages.lore.mender_hello_01_v05.text: I'll listen as soon as this stitch stops arguing.
messages.lore.mender_hello_01_v06.text: A moment, please. The seam has had more to say than the customer.
messages.lore.mender_magic_01.text: An old enchantment can keep doing its job after everyone forgets what the job was.
messages.lore.mender_magic_01_v02.text: Some enchantments keep working long after anyone remembers why they were made.
messages.lore.mender_magic_01_v03.text: An old working can outlast its instructions. That's when people bring it to me.
messages.lore.mender_magic_01_v04.text: The maker dies, the job is forgotten, and the spell carries on. It can make repairs complicated.
messages.lore.mender_magic_01_v05.text: I ask what an enchantment was meant to do before I decide what has gone wrong.
messages.lore.mender_magic_01_v06.text: A spell can be perfectly obedient to an order nobody needs anymore.
messages.lore.mender_neighbors_01.text: Two households can spend a year arguing over a gate and still ask the same mender to fix it. I send each of them half the bill.
messages.lore.mender_neighbors_01_v02.text: A disputed gate still needs a sound hinge. I charge each household for half.
messages.lore.mender_neighbors_01_v03.text: Neighbors arguing over a gate agree on one thing: I should mend it. Then they argue about the bill.
messages.lore.mender_neighbors_01_v04.text: I've repaired a gate while both households explained why it belonged to the other.
messages.lore.mender_neighbors_01_v05.text: Two households can disagree over a gate for years. The wood doesn't improve while they wait.
messages.lore.mender_neighbors_01_v06.text: I mend the shared gate, send half the bill each way, and let the neighbors choose what to argue about next.
messages.lore.mender_supper_active.text: Supper is being set out. I inspect a cup before I fill it. Occupational habit.
messages.lore.mender_supper_active_v02.text: Supper is going out. I always check a cup's rim before using it.
messages.lore.mender_supper_active_v03.text: They're setting supper by the fountain. I'll look for cracks before I pour anything.
messages.lore.mender_supper_active_v04.text: The table is being laid. A quick look at the cups won't delay me long.
messages.lore.mender_supper_active_v05.text: Supper's on its way out. I can't quite stop checking the handles.
messages.lore.mender_supper_active_v06.text: We're setting out a meal. I trust a cup more once I've turned it in my hand.
messages.lore.mender_supper_finished.text: Supper has finished. Warm cups cool at their own pace. So do people.
messages.lore.mender_supper_finished_v02.text: The meal is over. Let the cups cool before putting them away.
messages.lore.mender_supper_finished_v03.text: Supper's finished. The cups and their users can take their time cooling down.
messages.lore.mender_supper_finished_v04.text: The table has emptied. I leave a warm cup alone for a little while.
messages.lore.mender_supper_finished_v05.text: After supper, even a good cup deserves time on the shelf.
messages.lore.mender_supper_finished_v06.text: We've finished eating. There's no hurry to pack warm cups together.
messages.lore.mender_world_01.text: That hinge came from a world with no iron. This door came from a world with too much of it. They fit. Took me most of a morning.
messages.lore.mender_world_01_v02.text: I fitted an ironless world's hinge to a door from a world full of iron. It took most of the morning.
messages.lore.mender_world_01_v03.text: That door and its hinge began in different worlds. One had too much iron, one had none. I made them meet by lunchtime.
messages.lore.mender_world_01_v04.text: The hinge came from a world without iron. The door didn't. Most of a morning went into making them agree.
messages.lore.mender_world_01_v05.text: Different worlds made that hinge and door. Their makers never had to worry about fitting them together. I did.
messages.lore.mender_world_01_v06.text: I spent most of the morning with a hinge from an ironless world and a door from one that had too much. They close properly now.
messages.lore.milewarden_delivery_active.text: There is a local delivery to sort. Every crate has a mark. I wish everyone marked their maps this clearly.
messages.lore.milewarden_delivery_active_v02.text: They're sorting the delivery. Every crate has a legible mark. What a comfort.
messages.lore.milewarden_delivery_active_v03.text: The crates are being put in order. I'd like their marker to write on my maps.
messages.lore.milewarden_delivery_active_v04.text: A delivery to sort, and someone has labeled it properly. I appreciate that.
messages.lore.milewarden_delivery_active_v05.text: The delivery marks are clear. If only every road account were as easy to follow.
messages.lore.milewarden_delivery_active_v06.text: They're sorting the crates in the square. A good mark saves a great deal of pointing.
messages.lore.milewarden_delivery_finished.text: The delivery has been received. The crates are still in the square. I recorded where they stand; nobody asked me to.
messages.lore.milewarden_delivery_finished_v02.te: The delivery's arrived. I've written where the crates stand, though nobody required a map of them.
messages.lore.milewarden_delivery_finished_v03.te: The crates are still in the square after delivery. I found myself noting their positions.
messages.lore.milewarden_delivery_finished_v04.te: Delivery received. I've made a small plan of the crate stacks. Habit.
messages.lore.milewarden_delivery_finished_v05.te: The crates have arrived and stayed put. I recorded their positions before realizing I had no reason to.
messages.lore.milewarden_delivery_finished_v06.te: The square has received its delivery. My notes about where it stands are more precise than anyone asked for.
messages.lore.milewarden_supper_active.text: Supper by the fountain. I can keep a map folded for the length of a meal. Usually.
messages.lore.milewarden_supper_active_v02.text: There's supper by the fountain. The map can stay folded until I've eaten.
messages.lore.milewarden_supper_active_v03.text: A meal by the fountain is a useful reason to put my papers away.
messages.lore.milewarden_supper_active_v04.text: We're having supper here. I shall try to leave the road out of the conversation for one bowl.
messages.lore.milewarden_supper_active_v05.text: Supper is being set out. My map fits in its pocket better than beside a plate.
messages.lore.milewarden_supper_active_v06.text: The fountain table is being laid. I've folded the map; that ought to count as being ready.
messages.lore.milewarden_supper_finished.text: Supper is over. I learned that three people can disagree about a road without unfolding a single map.
messages.lore.milewarden_supper_finished_v02.text: The meal is over. We managed a road argument with every map still folded.
messages.lore.milewarden_supper_finished_v03.text: Supper finished before the argument about the road did.
messages.lore.milewarden_supper_finished_v04.text: We ate by the fountain. Several people disagreed about a road they'd never put on paper.
messages.lore.milewarden_supper_finished_v05.text: The dishes are clearing. I've learned that folded maps don't prevent route disputes.
messages.lore.milewarden_supper_finished_v06.text: Supper's done. I kept the map away from the food, though I couldn't keep roads out of the talk.
messages.lore.potfolk_bye_01_v03.text: May the road treat you carefully.
messages.lore.potfolk_bye_01_v04.text: Good roads. Watch the hard corners.
messages.lore.potfolk_bye_01_v05.text: Travel safely. I'm fond of an uneventful arrival.
messages.lore.potfolk_bye_01_v06.text: Mind your footing. I'll mind mine.
messages.lore.potfolk_handle_01.text: I chose this handle. The first one was somebody else's idea.
messages.lore.potfolk_handle_01_v02.text: This handle was my choice. The one I started with wasn't.
messages.lore.potfolk_handle_01_v03.text: Someone else picked my first handle. I picked this one myself.
messages.lore.potfolk_handle_01_v04.text: I chose the handle I'm wearing now. It took a while for anyone to ask.
messages.lore.potfolk_handle_01_v05.text: My first handle came with me. This one came from a decision I made.
messages.lore.potfolk_handle_01_v06.text: I had a say in this handle. I'd like that remembered.
messages.lore.potfolk_hello_01.text: I'm the courier. The soup is a separate arrangement.
messages.lore.potfolk_hello_01_v02.text: I'm here to deliver a message. Soup requires a separate agreement.
messages.lore.potfolk_hello_01_v03.text: Courier. Please address the letter, not the soup.
messages.lore.potfolk_hello_01_v04.text: I carry letters for a living. What I carry for supper is my business.
messages.lore.potfolk_hello_01_v05.text: I'm the courier you were waiting for. You weren't promised soup.
messages.lore.potfolk_hello_01_v06.text: The delivery is a letter. Any soup is between me and the cook.
messages.lore.quest_borrowed_light.author: The local archive of {city_name}
messages.lore.quest_borrowed_light.completion: So they called it their own. My grandmother would have had words with them. I'll keep your copy beside ours. Let the next reader see both.
messages.lore.quest_borrowed_light.finding: Here the lamp is borrowed. There it belongs to whoever tends it. The two places kept different customs.
messages.lore.quest_borrowed_light.inscription: The keeper who tends this lamp owns it. After the keeper departs, the lamp passes to the next keeper as their own property.
messages.lore.quest_borrowed_light.ledger_prompt: Copy the lamp account from the town book in {city_name} before setting out.
messages.lore.quest_borrowed_light.target.label: Archive inscription
messages.lore.quest_borrowed_light.text: You're a Milewarden, aren't you? Perhaps you can settle an argument. We pass a lamp from house to house, but the inscription in {dungeon_name} may tell a different story. Read our ledger before you go, then bring me the words you find there.
messages.lore.quest_borrowed_light.title: Whose Light Remains
messages.lore.quest_returned_names.author: The local archive of {city_name}
messages.lore.quest_returned_names.completion: They left the choice to the traveler too. Good. I was hoping we hadn't forgotten something kind.
messages.lore.quest_returned_names.finding: Both registers let the traveler choose what to write on returning. Both allow the line to stay empty.
messages.lore.quest_returned_names.inscription: At departure the name is entered. At return the traveler may add a name or leave the second line empty.
messages.lore.quest_returned_names.ledger_prompt: Copy the returning-name account from the town book in {city_name} before setting out.
messages.lore.quest_returned_names.target.label: Archive inscription
messages.lore.quest_returned_names.text: We leave a space after every traveler's name. Some say the old archive in {dungeon_name} did the same. Your guild goes to places the rest of us only talk about. Would you copy our register, read theirs, and tell me what you find?
messages.lore.quest_returned_names.title: A Space After the Name
messages.lore.quest_shared_measure.author: The local archive of {city_name}
messages.lore.quest_shared_measure.completion: Water and a place to sit. I'm glad those words lasted. I'll put your copy in the town book. Sit down while I find the ink.
messages.lore.quest_shared_measure.finding: Water and a place to rest count in both accounts. The old wardens used the same measure here and there.
messages.lore.quest_shared_measure.inscription: A measure is entered only where water is offered and a traveler can rest.
messages.lore.quest_shared_measure.ledger_prompt: Copy the shared-measure account from the town book in {city_name} before setting out.
messages.lore.quest_shared_measure.target.label: Archive inscription
messages.lore.quest_shared_measure.text: The old wardens measured a road by the places where you could drink and rest. That's how our town book tells it. If your travels take you to {dungeon_name}, will you copy the archive inscription? Read our account first. I'd like to know whether they counted as we did.
messages.lore.quest_shared_measure.title: The Third Measure
messages.lore.shade_attack_01.text: Stay where I can remember you.
messages.lore.skeleton_memory_01.text: There were beds here. I counted them.
messages.lore.warden_amber_01.text: A full cup deserves a steady hand.
messages.lore.warden_amber_01_v03.text: Keep the water steady before you hurry.
messages.lore.warden_amber_01_v04.text: A spilled cup is costly country out here.
messages.lore.warden_amber_01_v05.text: Take your time with a full vessel.
messages.lore.warden_amber_01_v06.text: Water is worth a steadier step.
messages.lore.warden_bye_01.text: If you find more country, write down how you reached it.
messages.lore.warden_bye_01_v02.text: Bring back the route as well as the name.
messages.lore.warden_bye_01_v03.text: Write how you got there. Someone will want to follow.
messages.lore.warden_bye_01_v04.text: Keep a note of the turns you take.
messages.lore.warden_bye_01_v05.text: If the road reaches unfamiliar country, leave a useful account.
messages.lore.warden_bye_01_v06.text: Good travels, guildmate. Give your return route a page too.
messages.lore.warden_dawn_01.text: The Office promised a complete map. We are still correcting their work.
messages.lore.warden_dawn_01_v02.text: The Office called its atlas final. Our margins keep growing.
messages.lore.warden_dawn_01_v03.text: An Office clerk promised the last map. I'd like to show them my extra sheets.
messages.lore.warden_dawn_01_v04.text: We still find the Office's old marks. We still have to check them.
messages.lore.warden_dawn_01_v05.text: The Office meant to finish the map during the Dawn. The roads have been uncooperative ever since.
messages.lore.warden_dawn_01_v06.text: Old Office maps have room for certainty. I prefer a margin for corrections.
messages.lore.warden_green_01.text: The oldest oaks still wear the surveyors' nails.
messages.lore.warden_green_01_v02.text: Some old oaks have grown around the survey nails.
messages.lore.warden_green_01_v03.text: Those copper marks went into the trees before our maps.
messages.lore.warden_green_01_v04.text: The trees have kept the oldest survey marks.
messages.lore.warden_green_01_v05.text: An oak can hold a surveyor's nail longer than a book holds its page.
messages.lore.warden_green_01_v06.text: Look for old nails where the bark has grown thick.
messages.lore.warden_guild_01.text: We Milewardens map the roads and catalogue the mysteries along them. Copy what you find. Ask who remembers it. Leave the next guildmate a way home.
messages.lore.warden_guild_01_v02.text: Milewardens bring back routes and accounts of strange things along them. A useful report helps the next traveler come home.
messages.lore.warden_guild_01_v03.text: Our guild maps the world and catalogues its mysteries. Write the place down before you get lost admiring it.
messages.lore.warden_guild_01_v04.text: We carry maps out and bring corrections home. If you find something strange, copy what you can and name who told you the rest.
messages.lore.warden_guild_01_v05.text: A Milewarden's journal holds roads, mysteries, and other people's accounts. Keep enough detail for a guildmate to follow your steps.
messages.lore.warden_guild_01_v06.text: We're here to map what we reach and learn what lives there. The next guildmate deserves more than a dramatic name.
messages.lore.warden_hello_01.text: Another Milewarden! I've put {city_name} on my map. Spelled it correctly this time.
messages.lore.warden_hello_01_v02.text: A Milewarden in {city_name}. Good. I'd like another pair of eyes on this map.
messages.lore.warden_hello_01_v03.text: Welcome, guildmate. I've written {city_name} clearly enough for once.
messages.lore.warden_hello_01_v04.text: {city_name} is on my map. Now there's another Milewarden to check the spelling.
messages.lore.warden_hello_01_v05.text: You've reached {city_name}, guildmate. Keep that name somewhere the rain won't find it.
messages.lore.warden_hello_01_v06.text: A fellow Milewarden! I've just finished putting {city_name} in the right margin.
messages.lore.warden_hello_02.text: A guildmate. Good. Hold this corner of the map before the wind takes it.
messages.lore.warden_hello_02_v02.text: Guildmate, could you hold this map flat? It wants to travel before I do.
messages.lore.warden_hello_02_v03.text: A Milewarden. Good company for an unfinished map.
messages.lore.warden_hello_02_v04.text: Come here, guildmate. This corner keeps folding over the place I'm trying to read.
messages.lore.warden_hello_02_v05.text: Another journal on the road. Let me keep the wind off it.
messages.lore.warden_hello_02_v06.text: Good to see a fellow Milewarden. Have you found a way to make paper ignore the weather?
messages.lore.warden_neighbors_01.text: An old border can outlive the kingdom that drew it. I ask the neighbors what they call a place before I put ink on the map.
messages.lore.warden_neighbors_01_v02.text: Before I copy an old border, I ask who lives on each side of it.
messages.lore.warden_neighbors_01_v03.text: A kingdom can vanish while its boundary stones remain. The neighbors still have to get along.
messages.lore.warden_neighbors_01_v04.text: Two neighbors may name a place differently. My map has room for both names.
messages.lore.warden_neighbors_01_v05.text: I write down what the people here call their country. Old rulers rarely answer follow-up questions.
messages.lore.warden_neighbors_01_v06.text: A border on old paper is worth asking about. So are the households it crosses.
messages.lore.warden_ruin_01.text: There is a ruin called {dungeon_name} in the country near {city_name}.
messages.lore.warden_ruin_01_v02.text: My notes place {dungeon_name} in the country near {city_name}.
messages.lore.warden_ruin_01_v03.text: There's an old ruin near {city_name} called {dungeon_name}. I've written down the name.
messages.lore.warden_ruin_01_v04.text: {dungeon_name} is the ruin named in my notes for the country around {city_name}.
messages.lore.warden_ruin_01_v05.text: If you're asking about ruins near {city_name}, I have an account naming {dungeon_name}.
messages.lore.warden_ruin_01_v06.text: I keep {dungeon_name} beside {city_name} in my road notes. That's the ruin people here refer to.
messages.lore.warden_world_01.text: The multiverse collapsed into the Endless World. Every road we follow belongs to it now. I've filled nine maps and still haven't found a good place to stop.
messages.lore.warden_world_01_v02.text: Countless worlds became the Endless World when the multiverse collapsed. I've filled nine maps of it. There's more road ahead.
messages.lore.warden_world_01_v03.text: The collapse joined the multiverse into one infinite world. Nine maps haven't made much of a dent in my pile of blank paper.
messages.lore.warden_world_01_v04.text: We walk one world now, made from the worlds that collapsed together. I've filled nine maps and kept walking.
messages.lore.warden_world_01_v05.text: The Endless World is what remains of the collapsed multiverse. I have nine maps of places I've reached, and room for another.
messages.lore.warden_world_01_v06.text: The multiverse came together in a single infinite world. Nine finished maps are sitting in my bag. The world is still ahead of me.
